messages.subject: nested BYM model
parts:
Hello INLA users! 
I'm working with models with BYM random effects. The response variable (O) is usually distributed as a Poisson (mu.O). 
In my particular case, I’m working with two independent response variables O1 and O2, and I would like to model them jointly as a nested model, I mean: 
O1 ∼ Poisson(mu.O1)
 log(mu.O1) = log(E1) + intercept_1 + BYM_1 

O2 ∼ Poisson(mu.O2) 
log(mu.O2) = log(E2) + intercept_2 + BYM_1 + BYM_2 

How can I fit this model using INLA? 
Thanks in advance :) 
Lidia

parts: Write a joint model and use NA to zero out the BYM_2 contribution  to O1. If BYM1 and 2, has the same precision, its slightly different: using copy.

Subject: [r-inla] nested BYM model

 

 

Hello INLA users! 

I'm working with models with BYM random effects. The response variable (O) is usually distributed as a Poisson (mu.O). 

In my particular case, I’m working with two independent response variables O1 and O2, and I would like to model them jointly as a nested model, I mean: 

O1 ∼ Poisson(mu.O1)

 log(mu.O1) = log(E1) + intercept_1 + BYM_1 

 

O2 ∼ Poisson(mu.O2) 

log(mu.O2) = log(E2) + intercept_2 + BYM_1 + BYM_2 

 

How can I fit this model using INLA? 

Thanks in advance :) 

Lidia

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] nested BYM model
parts:
the code would be something like

n = length(O1)
Y = c(O1, O2)
intercept = as.factor(c(rep(1,n), rep(2,n))
E = c(E1, E2)

idx1 = c(1:n,1:n)
idx2 = c(rep(NA,n), 1:n)

formula = Y ~ -1 + intercept + f(idx1, model="bym", graph=g) + f(idx2,
model="bym", graph=g)

inla(formula, data = data.frame(Y,intercept,E,idx1,idx2), E=E,
family = "poisson")

for bym1 and bym2 having two different precisions.
